highlights.title: Round basals to pump's actual supported rates
changes: Basal recommendations are now rounded against the actual paired pump's supported rates.
The pump is handed a bit-exact rate to avoid tiny numeric errors lowering the delivered dose.
An obsolete stored pump model setting was removed so the app no longer falls back to a bundled default.
This prevents unintended small drops in delivered basal rates for affected pumps.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1429: Fix Pump Basal Rate Rounding
Round basal rates with the pump's own rate table
Hand the pump a bit-exact basal rate

highlights.title: Fix battery update after switching pumps
changes: Battery percent now updates after switching or onboarding a pump without restarting the app.
The home-screen battery icon shows the new pump's battery immediately after a swap.
The simulator seeds an initial battery row so a battery appears before its first status update.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1430: Fix pump battery not updating after pumpmanager swap
Persist pump battery from the delegate callback instead of a status observer

highlights.title: Remove Medtronic Enlite CGM
changes: The Medtronic Enlite CGM option is removed from CGM device lists and settings.
Trio will no longer attempt to fetch glucose data from Enlite/Minilink devices.
Enlite-related names and localized strings have been removed from the app.
Enlite is no longer available as a selectable CGM type in setup sheets and dialogs.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix Pump Basal Rate Rounding
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

As reported in #1424, `TempBasalFunctions.roundBasal` erroneously considered every pump to one hardcoded set of supported basal rates, 0.025 below 1 U/hr, 0.05 to 10, 0.1 above, which is actually a Medtronic x23/x54’s rate... Further, `profile.model` was read from `settings/model.json`, a file that was never ever written to disk. As a consequence, every algorithm run fell back to the bundled `"722"`

  ### Changes

  1. **Drop the unused pump model setting.** `Profile.model`, both `ProfileGenerator parameters, the `createProfiles` load, `Settings.model`, and the bundled `settings/model.json`.
  2. **Round with the actual pump's own supported rates.** `roundBasal` floors against a new non-persisted
     `Profile.supportedBasalRates`, injected per algorithm run from the paired driver in `OpenAPS.determineBasal`. This mirrors LoopKit's `PumpManager.roundToSupportedBasalRate`, so the rate the algorithm commits to is the rate the pump delivers / can actually deliver.
  3. **Round the closed-loop dose before delivery as an additional safety net.** `performBasal` and `performBolus` handed the determination to the driver unrounded, unlike their `enactTempBasal` / `enactBolus` twins in APSManager.

Adjusted unit tests accordingly.

Fixes #1424.

### Update

@mountrcg found that point 3 was wrong: `Foundation`'s `Decimal` → `Double` conversion can land just below the value (0.07 becomes 0.06999999999999999), and since every pump table floors, re-rounding at delivery dropped a full increment on 41 of Dana's 301 rates. Two follow-up commits:

- **Hand the pump a bit-exact rate.** `performBasal` / `performBolus` now convert via the decimal string, which is bit-identical to the driver's own table entry, and no longer re-floor — the algorithm already floored against the same table. The `roundToSupportedBasalRate` comparison stays as a log-only canary. The algorithm side was never affected: it stays in `Decimal` end to end.
- **Fix a test type-check timeout on Xcode 26.2**, which CI pins. Both jobs are green.

`BasalRoundingDriverParityTests` now walks every entry of all five kit tables through the real delivery path, with a regression pin on 0.07 / 0.14 / 1.99 against `Double(truncating:)`.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix pump battery not updating after pumpmanager swap
includedPullRequests.body:
BaseAPSManager registers itself as a PumpManagerStatusObserver at init. This means if the pump manager is replaced without an app relaunch (i.e. switching pumps) the observer stays bound to the previous instance.

The delegate is re-attached in DeviceDataManager's didSet, so reservoir/dose/status data kept flowing, but the observer-driven storeBatteryStatus never ran for the new pump -- no OpenAPS_Battery rows were written and the home battery icon stayed hidden until relaunch.

Fix by having DeviceDataManager emitspumpManagerDidChange from the pumpManager didSet (where the delegate is already re-attached), covering every assignment path. APSManager re-registers its status observer on that signal.

includedPullRequests.title: Remove Enlite CGM
includedPullRequests.body: Medtronic stopped production on their MiniMed Enlite CGM back in 2020, which had a 6-month warranty... so if anyone has any of these sensors today they are very expired and likely very untrustworthy. Furthermore, its functionality has never been validated in Trio, as no Trio developer has had access to the hardware to test with it.
